prompt: What does `react-native-screens` add to React Navigation?

choices.text: The tab bar's icons
choices.why: Icons come from an icon library.

choices.text: Deep links to every screen of the app, configured automatically from the file names
choices.why: Links come from the `linking` object; file names are Expo Router's way.

choices.text: Each screen as a real native screen
choices.why: Right: a UIViewController on iOS, a Fragment on Android.

choices.text: A web server for the export
choices.why: Serving is another tool's job.

prompt: Match each navigator with what the person sees.

pairs.right: a bar of screens that keep their place

prompt: Why is the Course screen in the root stack rather than inside a tab?

choices.text: It covers the tab bar, and back returns to the tab
choices.why: Right: that is what nesting it above the tabs gives.

choices.text: Tabs cannot hold screens with params
choices.why: They can.

choices.text: Native stacks render faster than tabs
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: Deep links only work for stack screens
choices.why: `/week` opened a tab.

prompt: In this lesson, why do the screens import `courses.json` themselves instead of receiving the plan?

choices.text: Props are forbidden in React Navigation
choices.why: Not forbidden; the navigator just passes its own.

choices.text: It is faster to read a file per screen
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: TypeScript cannot type a plan passed through a navigator
choices.why: It could, through params, but params should be ids.

choices.text: A navigator passes only `navigation` and `route`
choices.why: Right; lesson 9 moves the plan into shared state.

prompt: A course is passed to its screen as `{ course }`, then renamed. What does the open screen show?

choices.text: The new name, because objects are passed by reference and React tracks them
choices.why: The planner's rules return new objects; the old copy is what the screen holds.

choices.text: The old name
choices.why: Right: params are a copy taken at the press.

choices.text: An error
choices.why: Nothing fails; it is quietly stale.

choices.text: Nothing, the screen closes
choices.why: It stays open.

prompt: What should the Course screen do with an id that matches no course?

choices.text: Throw, so the bug is noticed
choices.why: An old link is not a bug in the app; the person needs an answer.

choices.text: Say plainly there is no such course
choices.why: Right, as `/course/chemistry` showed.

choices.text: Show the first course instead
choices.why: That shows the wrong thing without saying so.

choices.text: Go back silently
choices.why: The person would not know why.

prompt: A screen reads what it was given from `route.___`.
`npx expo serve` answered `/course/guitar` with 404. What does a single-page app need from its server?

choices.text: A file for every course, generated at export
choices.why: Not for a single-page app.

choices.text: A redirect from every path to `/`, which keeps the person on the course list
choices.why: A redirect loses the path the app needs to read.

choices.text: HTTPS
choices.why: Unrelated to the 404.

choices.text: `index.html` for every path
choices.why: Right: the app then reads the path, as `serve --single` allows.

prompt: Why is `planner://` not enough for a link sent by email that must open only your app?

choices.text: Nothing stops another app claiming it
choices.why: Right; App Links and Universal Links tie an https address to your app.

choices.text: Email clients strip custom schemes
choices.why: Not the security problem the section names.

choices.text: Custom schemes work only on the web
choices.why: They work on phones.

choices.text: `planner` is reserved by Apple
choices.why: No.

prompt: Which part of the linking config makes `/week` open the second tab?

choices.text: `prefixes`, which lists the schemes the app answers
choices.why: That is the scheme, not a path.

choices.text: `Course: "course/:id"`
choices.why: That is the Course screen.

choices.text: `Week: "week"` inside `Tabs`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `Courses: ""`
choices.why: That is the first tab.

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer `beforeRemove` over Android's `BackHandler` to protect a half-filled form?

choices.text: It covers every way of leaving, on both platforms
choices.why: Right: the header button, the swipe and Android's back.

choices.text: `BackHandler` was removed in React Native 0.82
choices.why: It still exists.

choices.text: It saves the form's contents to the device
choices.why: It only stops the navigation.

choices.text: It works without a navigator
choices.why: The reverse: it is a navigator event.

prompt: On the first tab, a person presses Android's back. What does the platform's convention expect?

choices.text: Nothing happens
choices.why: Back always does something.

choices.text: The last tab opens
choices.why: Back does not cycle tabs.

choices.text: The app is left
choices.why: Right: back goes where they came from, or out.

choices.text: A confirmation dialog asks whether to quit
choices.why: Not the convention.

prompt: Put in order what happens when `/course/guitar` is opened in the browser.
items: the app loads and reads the path
linking turns it into the Course route with `id: guitar`
the screen looks the course up by id

prompt: Which of these belong in a route's params? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: a course's id
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: the whole plan
choices.why: A copy that goes stale, and too large.

choices.text: a callback to call when done
choices.why: Functions cannot be saved or put in an address.

choices.text: a session's id
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: A notification opens `planner://course/guitar`. The person presses back and the app closes. What would put the course list underneath?

choices.text: Passing the whole plan in the link
choices.why: Params should be ids, and this is about the stack.

choices.text: `initialRouteName` in the linking config
choices.why: Right: the tabs go under the deep-linked screen.

choices.text: A second scheme registered for notifications
choices.why: Unrelated.

choices.text: A `BackHandler` that reopens the app
choices.why: That fights the platform.
